Position SummaryThe Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences (EPS) at the University of New Mexico (UNM) invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor position in Stable Isotope Geochemistry to begin in August 2027. Applicants must have a Ph.D. in geochemistry, geology, Earth and planetary sciences, chemistry, or a closely related discipline by the start date of the appointment. For best consideration, all application materials must be received by December 13, 2026. We seek a scientist who uses stable isotopic methods to address fundamental questions about Earth or other planetary systems. The successful candidate will develop an independent, externally funded research program in stable isotope geochemistry and contribute to the intellectual environment and technical capabilities of the UNM Center for Stable Isotopes (CSI). The successful candidate will bring hands-on experience with stable isotope instrumentation, laboratory techniques, and analytical workflows, ideally including isotope-ratio mass spectrometry (IRMS) and one or more laser-based approaches, such as laser spectroscopy, laser fluorination, laser ablation, compound-specific isotope analysis, or related methods. They will also have opportunities to contribute to our two-week summer course, IsoCamp (isocamp.org), and pursue a leadership role in CSI. CSI is an interdisciplinary research and analytical facility supporting stable isotope research across Earth and Planetary Sciences, Biology, Anthropology, Chemistry, and the Biomedical Sciences. The center provides broad access to instrumentation for measuring stable isotopes of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, hydrogen, sulfur, and chlorine in organic and inorganic materials, as well as hands-on training in sample collection, preparation, analysis, and data interpretation.
